title: Water Disinfection: Boiling & Heat Pasteurization
summary: Gold standard thermal disinfection method for eliminating pathogenic bacteria, viruses, and protozoan parasites from raw water.
contentMarkdown:
# Water Boiling Protocol

Boiling is the most reliable method to kill disease-causing microorganisms, including Giardia, Cryptosporidium, Salmonella, and Vibrio cholerae.

### Altitude Adjustment
* Sea level up to 1,000 meters (3,300 ft): 1 full rolling boil minute is sufficient.
* Above 1,000 meters: Boil vigorously for 3 full minutes (water boils at lower temperature at high altitude).
steps: Clarify turbid water: If water contains silt or organic debris, filter through clean cloth, paper towel, or let it settle in a container for 30 minutes to decant clear water.
Bring to rolling boil: Heat clear water in a clean pot until large bubbles continuously break the surface vigorously.
Maintain timer: Maintain rolling boil for at least 1 full minute (3 minutes at elevations over 1,000 m / 3,300 ft).
Cool safely: Cover with a clean lid and allow to cool naturally. Store in a disinfected, sealed container.
Aerate for taste: Boiled water tastes flat; pour it repeatedly back and forth between two clean containers to reintroduce oxygen.
sourceManual: CDC & World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality

title: Chemical Disinfection: Household Chlorine Bleach
summary: Standard chemical chlorination ratio using unscented regular liquid household bleach (6% to 8.25% sodium hypochlorite).
contentMarkdown:
# Emergency Chemical Water Disinfection

When fuel or fire is unavailable for boiling, unscented plain household bleach can purify water for drinking.

### Critical Safety Rule
* NEVER use scented bleach, color-safe bleach, or bleach with added cleansers or fragrance—these contain toxic industrial additives.
steps: Check label: Verify the bottle says 'Regular Unscented Liquid Bleach' containing sodium hypochlorite (5%–9%).
Ratio for CLEAR water: Add 2 drops of regular bleach per 1 Liter (or 8 drops per 1 Gallon / 3.8 L) of clear water.
Ratio for CLOUDY or cold water: Add 4 drops of regular bleach per 1 Liter (or 16 drops per 1 Gallon) of turbid water.
Mix thoroughly: Stir or shake vigorously for 30 seconds.
Wait 30 minutes: Let the container stand tightly covered for at least 30 minutes before drinking.
Check odor: Water should have a very faint chlorine smell. If no chlorine scent is detected, repeat dose with half amount and wait another 15 minutes.
sourceManual: EPA Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water Guidelines

title: Solar Water Disinfection (SODIS Protocol)
summary: Low-cost ultraviolet and thermal pathogen destruction using clear PET plastic bottles and direct sunlight.
contentMarkdown:
# Solar Disinfection (SODIS)

UV-A rays from sunlight kill bacterial pathogens, viruses, and parasites through DNA damage and thermal heating inside transparent bottles.

### Equipment
* Clean, transparent PET plastic bottles (under 2 Liters, not colored, without scratches).
* Reflective surface (corrugated metal roof or aluminum foil) boosts efficiency.
steps: Clean bottle: Wash clean clear PET bottles thoroughly.
Fill with clear water: Fill bottle 3/4 full with clear water, cap tightly, and shake vigorously for 20 seconds to oxygenate.
Top off: Fill the remaining space to the brim and seal tightly.
Expose to direct sun: Place bottles horizontally on a reflective surface (e.g. tin roof) in direct unshaded sunlight.
Duration: Leave in direct full sun for at least 6 consecutive hours (or 2 full days if the sky is overcast / 50% cloud cover).
Consume directly: Drink straight from the bottle or pour into sterile cups to prevent recontamination.
sourceManual: Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science (Eawag) / WHO SODIS Manual

title: Improvised Charcoal & Sand Bio-Filter
summary: Constructing a multi-stage physical and chemical adsorption filter using charcoal, sand, and gravel in a container.
contentMarkdown:
# Improvised Bio-Sand Charcoal Filter

This filter removes suspended particulates, silt, heavy metals, odors, and organic impurities from muddy or turbid water. Note: physical filters do not kill microscopic viruses; water MUST be boiled or chlorinated after filtration.
steps: Prepare container: Cut the bottom off a plastic bottle, bamboo stalk, or bucket. Punch small drain holes in the cap or base.
Base layer: Stuff a clean cloth, cotton balls, or unbleached fabric at the spout to keep sand from escaping.
Activated charcoal layer: Crush hardwood charcoal (from non-toxic wood fire) into pea-sized bits. Add a 3 to 4 inch layer to absorb chemicals and odors.
Fine sand layer: Add 3 to 4 inches of clean fine sand above the charcoal.
Coarse gravel layer: Add 2 inches of small pebbles and gravel on top to catch large debris without disrupting the sand bed.
Run flush water: Slowly pour raw water through and discard the first 2-3 liters until output flows completely transparent.
Disinfect filtrate: Boil or chlorinate the clarified output before drinking.
sourceManual: US Army Survival Field Manual FM 21-76
